analysis.headline: US G60 customers still buy into the 5 Series for its driving character, but the product experience is being dragged down by HMI complexity, seat comfort, everyday practicality gaps, and EV-use friction.
analysis.summary: The strongest part of the US G60 is still the core BMW brief: handling, ride comfort, acceleration and overall driving performance are all strong in both verbatims and study scores. Customers repeatedly describe the car as smooth, sporty and luxurious. The main risk is that this strength is being diluted by too many daily-use irritants. The biggest product issues are not one single defect cluster but a set of high-frequency usability gaps: the operating concept is too menu-heavy, climate and common functions are harder to access than customers expect, seats are too firm or hard to adjust for many body types, storage and trunk convenience have regressed versus prior cars, and digital basics such as CarPlay, profiles and wireless charging do not feel robust enough. For BEV and PHEV users, electric range and charging confidence are also material pain points. First look should go to H1 actions that reduce friction in the current generation: simplify access to frequent functions, stabilize phone/profile behavior, improve seat comfort and adjustment, restore practical storage and convenience features, and improve EV guidance and charging experience. Protect the current ride/handling balance as a non-negotiable strength.
analysis.data_coverage: Analysis rests on the US market context pack plus 3,628 verbatims for US market scope (3,610 US, 18 CA in the pack), market findings, US_2025 study metrics, equipment catalogue entries, sales volumes, existing requirements and CPM effort outputs. Evidence is strongest for operating concept, seats, storage, climate, trunk access, drivetrain and electric-range topics because these have level A or B findings with 20-98 complaint rows and supporting study metrics in several cases. Strength evidence is also strong for driving dynamics, with 210 likes for Handling / Riding, 349 likes for Drivetrain, and study means of 6.058 for Handling/Maneuverability, 6.039 for Overall driving performance, 6.03 for Riding comfort and 6.026 for Acceleration from stop.

insights.title: Driving dynamics remain the core strength to protect
insights.statement: Driving experience is the clearest strength in the US. Handling / Riding has 210 likes, Drivetrain has 349 likes, and the study is strong on Handling/Maneuverability at 6.058, Overall driving performance at 6.039, Riding comfort at 6.03 and Acceleration from stop at 6.026. Complaint share in Driving Experience & Dynamics is relatively low at 30%, so the positive signal is broad, not marginal.
insights.customer_quote: excellent driving feel, really nice blend of sporty and luxury.

insights.title: The operating concept is a major usability drag, not just a learning curve issue
insights.statement: The operating concept is a level-A complaint with 53 complaint rows, 39 of them Difficult to Use, equal to 2.0% of all US complaint rows and 63% of all rows on that theme. This is reinforced by weak study scores for Menu structure of infotainment system at 4.879 and Operation of heater/ AC controls at 4.804. Customers repeatedly say common functions are buried in menus and that replacing physical controls with touch interaction takes attention off the road.
insights.customer_quote: the screen layout is not very intuitive for accessing some functions

insights.title: Seats are one of the biggest product weaknesses and affect both comfort and ergonomics
insights.statement: Seats are the largest interior complaint theme with 62 complaint rows, 13 defects and 33 usability problems, representing 2.4% of all US complaint rows. The issue is not only trim preference: customers report lower-back pain, firmness, insufficient adjustment range and awkward controls. Study support is clear, with Driver seat adjustability at 5.603, overall seat comfort cited in the existing requirement evidence, and rear seat comfort also flagged there as weak.
insights.customer_quote: the driver seat is extremely uncomfortable, especially in the lower back area

insights.title: Climate usability is weak and tied to the broader HMI problem
insights.statement: Climate is a practical daily-use issue rather than a niche complaint. Air conditioning, setting has 24 complaint rows at level A, and the study shows weak scores for Operation of heater/ AC controls at 4.804, Overall performance of climate control system at 5.144 and Air conditioner performance at 5.188. Customers also connect this to hidden controls and settings that are not direct enough.
insights.customer_quote: Customer stated that replacing physical buttons with more touch screens is a terrible trend

insights.title: Everyday practicality has regressed in storage and trunk convenience
insights.statement: Space & Practicality has the highest complaint share of any major domain at 78%. Within it, Storage compartments is a level-A unmet need with 28 complaint rows and Center console, front adds 30 complaint rows. Customers miss seat-back pockets, a sunglasses holder and larger glovebox/console storage. The hands-free trunk is another recurring pain point with 44 complaint rows, 39 of them usability problems, and customers compare it unfavorably with prior BMWs.
insights.customer_quote: There just isnt enough storage, and there is no dedicated overhead spot to keep sunglasses

insights.title: Phone integration and charging feel below premium expectations
insights.statement: Digital basics are not robust enough. Wireless charging has 26 complaint rows, including 11 defects, and Apple CarPlay has 37 complaint rows. Customers report wrong-phone connection by profile, slow or inconsistent charging, awkward tray geometry and audio/connectivity issues. This is supported by the existing requirement and a weak study signal for phone charging cited there.
insights.customer_quote: At times the car links to the wrong phone for the user profile

insights.title: EV customers want more range and more trustworthy range guidance
insights.statement: Electric Range is a level-B recurring complaint with 67 complaint rows, 50 of them usability problems, and 64% of all rows on that theme are complaints. The issue is both absolute range and confidence in the estimate, especially in cold weather. Public charging / external providers adds 55 complaint rows, mostly BEV-related, showing that the ownership experience is constrained by charging compatibility and infrastructure as customers experience it.
insights.customer_quote: range estimates are off, the efficiency stats shown are basically made up

insights.title: Auto start-stop is a concentrated ICE irritation with a clear customer ask
insights.statement: Automatic engine start-stop function (MSA) has 45 complaint rows, 32 of them usability problems and 11 wishes, and 96% of all rows on that theme are complaints. This is a focused issue rather than a diffuse one: customers explicitly ask for a persistent off option and some link the function to comfort loss when the air-conditioning cuts back.
insights.customer_quote: there is also no option to turn off the auto start/stop.

insights.title: Technology richness is valued, but complexity is high enough to need onboarding support
insights.statement: The broad 'overall technology' theme is mixed rather than simply negative: 98 complaints but also 201 likes. That means customers do value the feature set, yet many feel overwhelmed by it. Several verbatims describe the car as feature-rich but hard to master, suggesting that some pain can be reduced by better guided onboarding as well as by simplifying the HMI itself.
insights.customer_quote: the tech in this car feels like too much to learn.

recommendations.title: Simplify access to frequent functions in the current generation
recommendations.proposal: Consider prioritising a current-generation HMI simplification package so the most-used functions are reachable in one touch or via direct controls where the panel allows it, with climate, seat heating, steering-wheel heating, drive mode, assistance on/off, map and phone first.
recommendations.rationale: This addresses one of the strongest and best-supported pain points: 53 operating-concept complaints, weak infotainment menu-structure and climate-control usability scores, and repeated customer requests for fewer menu layers and more direct access. Existing requirement coverage is already in place.

recommendations.title: Improve seat comfort and adjustment range for US use cases
recommendations.proposal: Consider an H1 seat package focused on softer long-distance comfort, flatter lumbar calibration, and adjustment ranges that better cover shorter drivers and visibility/HUD alignment needs.
recommendations.rationale: Seats are the largest interior complaint theme and the issue is functional, not cosmetic: pain, firmness and adjustment range recur across sources. The stored CPM estimate for the existing requirement is an adaptation-level effort only, but that estimate is model-based and uncalibrated, so it should be used only as a rough prioritisation factor.

recommendations.title: Make climate control more direct and persistent
recommendations.proposal: Consider combining HMI and HVAC updates so climate temperature and fan are always visible or directly accessible, key settings persist by profile, and cabin cool-down performance is tuned for US heat-soak conditions.
recommendations.rationale: Climate complaints are frequent enough to matter daily and are backed by weak study scores. This is also one of the clearer places where HMI friction and functional performance meet. Existing requirement coverage is already defined.

recommendations.title: Restore everyday storage and convenience features customers miss
recommendations.proposal: Consider an H1 practicality update that restores or adds the small-item storage features customers explicitly miss, especially seat-back pockets, a sunglasses holder and more usable covered console/glovebox storage.
recommendations.rationale: Space & Practicality has the highest complaint share, and the storage complaints are highly specific and repeated. This is a tangible way to improve daily satisfaction without changing the vehicle concept. Existing requirement coverage is already present.

recommendations.title: Stabilise phone integration and wireless charging behavior
recommendations.proposal: Consider a digital-quality H1 package that binds CarPlay/phone connection more reliably to the active profile, aligns source loudness, and improves wireless charging tray usability and thermal robustness.
recommendations.rationale: These are premium-basics failures: wrong phone pairing, slow or inconsistent charging and awkward tray use. Complaint counts are smaller than the HMI theme overall, but defect share is meaningful, especially for wireless charging. Existing requirement coverage is already defined.

recommendations.title: Improve EV confidence now, and plan a larger range step for the successor
recommendations.proposal: Consider a two-step response for EV customers: in H1, improve range prediction, winter guidance and charging-route confidence; in H2, evaluate a materially larger real-world range step for the successor generation.
recommendations.rationale: Customers complain both about actual range and about trusting the estimate. The H1 software response is already captured in an existing requirement, while the larger range step is also already captured as an H2 requirement. The stored H2 effort estimate is very large and model-based, not measured, so it should guide horizon choice rather than invalidate the customer need.

recommendations.title: Offer a persistent driver-controlled off setting for auto start-stop
recommendations.proposal: Consider enabling a persistent off preference for MSA in driver profiles for ICE variants, with any necessary calibration checks handled in development.
recommendations.rationale: This is a concentrated, explicit customer ask with little ambiguity. It is not the biggest volume issue overall, but it is highly actionable and likely visible in satisfaction quickly. Existing requirement coverage is already present.

recommendations.title: Protect the current ride and handling balance through future changes
recommendations.proposal: Consider treating the current ride/handling character as a protected attribute in all updates and especially in the successor brief.
recommendations.rationale: This is the strongest positive equity in the US evidence. Customers forgive some complexity because the car still feels like a BMW to drive; losing that would remove the main offset to the usability issues.

assumptions_and_gaps: Country scope is market US, not US-only customer voice; the pack includes 18 Canadian verbatims among 3,628 total, though the effect is small at this scale.
Study metrics, sales and findings are market-level; they are not narrowed beyond US market scope.

The equipment catalogue is the German July 2026 price list, so it shows model-line availability rather than US standard/optional content. I therefore did not rely on it for US packaging conclusions except as portfolio context.

Sales notes say G60 volumes are reported on a combined G60/G68 sheet; for US this is still the provided evidence, but the note should be kept with any volume interpretation. The cited figures are 75,600 in 2024, 78,000 in 2025 and 80,000 plan in 2030.
Some verbatims, especially Source B call-centre notes, mix product feedback with process or coaching content. I used them only for the product signal, not as instructions.

The broad 'Body equipment, overall technology' theme is mixed, with many likes as well as complaints; this means not all complexity pain should be solved by removing features. Better onboarding may reduce part of the issue.

CPM effort outputs are assumptions from an uncalibrated model, not measured engineering effort. Where effort matters, it should be used only to choose horizon and packaging, not to judge whether the customer need is real.

I did not call search_documents because the user asked for a product situation analysis and the available market evidence already determined the priorities; BMW Group strategy passages would not materially change the product conclusions here.

effort.method: CPM, share of the development effort of a new vehicle generation; never money; every model input is an uncalibrated assumption (config/effort/model.yaml)

changes.why: Shortcut layer and widget placement for ten functions
Physical controls where the panel allows them
Front and rear cushion foam, contour and lumbar travel on the existing seat structure
Vent and blower tuning for heat-soak cool-down
Persist recirculation, sync and seat-ventilation defaults per profile
Seat-back pockets, sunglasses holder, covered tray, larger door pockets
CarPlay profile binding and loudness matching
New cell and pack generation for more range (same case as the Gen6 anchor)
Persistent off setting in the driver profile (OTA)
Restart calibration; certification credit check stays open (requirement uncertainty)

flags.text: borderline: only 69 % of the sensitivity runs keep the decision; show the PM both options
